notes.short: “A sword” stands for the strife His coming brings
notes.about: The sword is named for what it brings: strife. The next verse shows where it reaches, setting a man against his father and a daughter against her mother.

figure.name: Metonymy
figure.means: strife and division, even inside families

original.note: In Matthew's Greek the word is machaira, a sword.

notes.evidence: Bullinger names the figure in Figures of Speech and again in the Companion Bible: the sword is put for war. Barnes says to send a sword is to produce hostility and war, and Jamieson, Fausset and Brown explain it as strife and division.

cites.quote: “I came not to send peace, but a sword” (i.e., but for war). That is to say, the object of His coming was peace, but the effect of it was war.

cites.quote: Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Cause), App-6, for "war" or "fightings".

cites.quote: The sword is an instrument of death, and to send a sword is the same as to produce hostility and war.

cites.quote: strife, discord, conflict; deadly opposition between eternally hostile principles, penetrating into and rending asunder the dearest ties.
